Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr.Viveka Nandsingh  For the Respondent/s : Mr.A.G  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR PANDEY  ORAL ORDER 6 21-02-2023 Heard the parties.

The present memo of appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant for setting aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 11.11.2020 passed by Special Judge (POCSO)-cum-A.D.J.-VI Civil Court, Araria in Special POCSO Act Case No. 44 of 2017 arising out of Araria Mahila P.S. Case No. 70 of 2017 whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 4 of the POCSO Act and under Section 376(1), 313 of the Indian Penal Code and and accordingly, sentenced to undergo RI for a period of eight years and a fine of Rs. 25,000/- under Section 4 of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine the appellant has been further sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for three months.

sentences.text: Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1310 of 2021(6) dt.21-02-2023
As per prosecution case, the appellant has committed rape upon the informant's daughter.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is in jail since 24.10.2018 which is more than half of the punishment and appeal is not likely to be heard in near future.

There is a delay of five months in lodging the F.I.R. and no plausible explanation has been given for the delay in Arun Mandal@ Bhutwa Mandal vs The State Of Bihar on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144507103/
1 lodging the F.I.R.

sentences.text: The appellant is innocent and has committed no offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
There is contradictory statement of witnesses.
The statement of the informant in the F.I.R. and in the evidence in court is also contradictory to each other.

The learned counsel on behalf of the State vehemently opposes the prayer for bail of the appellant and submits that the order and judgment of sentence has been passed by the learned court is appropriate and just on the correct appreciation of evidences.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, period of custody already undergone by the appellants which is more than four years, appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, argument advanced on behalf of both sides as well as materials available on record, in the opinion of this Court it will be proper to enlarge the appellant on bail during the pendency of Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.1310 of 2021(6) dt.21-02-2023 the appeal

. 
Accordingly, let the appellant above-named be enlarged on bail during the pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) with two sureties of like amount each to the satisfaction of the Special Judge (POCSO)-cum-A.D.J.-VI Civil Court, Araria in Special POCSO Act Case No. 44 of 2017 arising out of Araria Mahila P.S. Case No. 70 of 2017.
Sentence of the appellant is suspended and realization of fine shall also remain stayed during the pendency of the appeal.
The appellant is directed to co-operate this Court in disposal of the appeal.
(Alok Kumar Pandey, J) amitkr/-
